pathway.title: MAXIMUS, INC. — Credit Snapshot
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: 1. Leverage is moderate but rising. Total debt principal is USD 1,653.5 million and unrestricted cash USD 57.0 million, so net debt is USD 1,596.6 million, or 2.25x LTM issuer-adjusted EBITDA of USD 711.0 million (2.33x gross), against 1.60x at September 30, 2025. Debt principal rose USD 306.7 million and net debt USD 472.1 million in nine months [CP-1 C5, C11]. 2. Covenant headroom is wide on the reported definition. Consolidated net total leverage is 2.00 against a 4.00 maximum, so Credit Agreement EBITDA of USD 798.4 million could fall 50.0% before the test binds, and net interest coverage is 8.72 against a 3.00 minimum, a 65.6% cushion. The Credit Agreement EBITDA exceeds the issuer-adjusted measure by USD 87.4 million of stock compensation and pro forma adjustments, and the agreement and its definitions are not supplied, so the headroom is the issuer's own figure [CP-1 C9; CP-0 gaps]. 3. Cash flow is seasonal and delayed. Operating cash flow was an outflow of USD 179.9 million in nine months and USD 469.5 million for the LTM, 66.0% of issuer-adjusted EBITDA. Days sales outstanding were 98 days against 62 because a large federal contract paid late; USD 245 million was collected after June 30, 2026. Full-year guidance implies fourth-quarter free cash flow of USD 633.6 million to USD 683.6 million, against USD 641.8 million delivered in the prior year's fourth quarter [CP-1 C3, C13; CP-1A]. 4. Shareholder returns are debt-funded. Nine-month buybacks of USD 204.9 million and dividends of USD 51.4 million, USD 256.4 million together, were met from net borrowing of USD 302.7 million and a USD 165.4 million fall in unrestricted cash, with other cash flows not itemised. Fiscal 2025 buybacks of USD 447.5 million were 6.5 times dividends. Management states a target leverage of 2x to 3x on the covenant definition, so the reported 2.00 sits at the bottom of the range [CP-1 C11; CP-1A governance]. 5. Liquidity is adequate but thin in cash. Liquidity is USD 787.0 million: cash USD 57.0 million plus USD 730.0 million of revolver capacity as printed, with letters of credit not stated and the USD 350.0 million receivable-sale facility excluded. Scheduled principal payments are USD 19.0 million for July to September 2026 and USD 75.8 million in fiscal 2027, covered 8.3 times by liquidity; the largest single-year bucket is USD 690.2 million in fiscal 2029 [CP-1 C10, maturities chart]. 6. Interest cost is exposed to floating rates. Swaps cover USD 675.0 million, 40.8% of principal; USD 978.5 million pays SOFR plus margin, so 100 basis points adds about USD 9.8 million a year. A USD 75.0 million Term Loan B swap expires in September 2026. The effective rate is 5.6% [CP-1 C12; C1 below]. 7. Earnings are down and the outlook was lowered. Nine-month revenue was USD 3,930.0 million, 4.4% lower, and fiscal Q3 revenue fell 5.1%, but issuer-adjusted EBITDA margin rose to 14.0% from 13.2%. In August 2026 adjusted EPS guidance fell to USD 7.90 to USD 8.20 from USD 8.25 to USD 8.55 and free cash flow guidance to USD 425 million to USD 475 million from USD 450 million to USD 500 million, after a customer modification effective July 1, 2026 through December 31, 2026 that management expects to reduce diluted EPS by about USD 0.35 per quarter [CP-1 latest quarter; CP-1A timeline]. 8. Revenue is concentrated and terminable. About 55% of fiscal 2025 revenue came from the U.S. federal government, about 60% from the ten largest contracts and about one-fifth from a single federal agency; almost all contracts permit termination for convenience. Backlog of USD 15,327 million is 2.82 times fiscal 2025 revenue but fell 5.2% in the year to September 30, 2025, and no later backlog is supplied [CP-1A operating model, C1, C2]. 9. Claims outside debt are modest but unquantified in places. Operating lease liabilities are USD 94.9 million; receivables of USD 1.28 billion were sold to a bank in nine months with the outstanding balance not printed; performance bonds were USD 33.2 million at September 30, 2025; the MOVEit litigation accrual is not stated; no defined benefit pension is described. Goodwill and intangibles exceed equity by USD 517.0 million [CP-1 claims table, C14]. 10. Governance is open on the facts that matter to creditors. There is no sponsor and no controlling holder disclosed (30 holders of record, about 151,000 beneficial owners), but the proxy statement, Credit Agreement, guarantors and change-of-control terms are not supplied, and three source conflicts are logged: the fiscal 2025 buyback amount, the federal revenue share definition and the Outside the U.S. margin outlook [CP-1A governance and conflicts].

runs.text: Strengths. Backlog and contract tenure: USD 15,327 million of backlog with about 5.0 years of average remaining life, including options, gives multi-year visibility [Documentary Fact; CP-1A operating model]. Simple, bank-only capital structure: one Credit Agreement with Term Loan A, Term Loan B and a USD 750 million revolver, with no bonds and scheduled principal payments below USD 100 million in each period before fiscal 2029 [Documentary Fact; CP-1 debt register]. Covenant headroom as reported: 2.00 against 4.00 and 8.72 against 3.00 [Documentary Fact, issuer-reported; CP-1]. Cash conversion over a full cycle: fiscal 2025 free cash flow of USD 366.2 million and LTM free cash flow of USD 433.2 million, which includes the prior year's strong fourth quarter [Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation; CP-1 C3]. Margin improvement: issuer-adjusted EBITDA margin of 14.0% in nine months against 13.2%, which management attributes to efficiency initiatives [Management Language; CP-1A operating model]. Light capital intensity: USD 28.8 million of capital expenditure in nine months [Documentary Fact; CP-1]. No sponsor extraction: no related-party leakage or creditor-adverse action is documented, though the legal documents are not supplied [Insufficient Information on legal capacity; CP-1A governance].

Weaknesses. Customer and contract concentration: about 60% of revenue from ten contracts, about 55% from the federal government, and termination for convenience in almost all contracts [Documentary Fact; CP-1A]. Seasonal and delayed cash flow: operating cash flow was an outflow of USD 179.9 million in nine months and days sales outstanding were 98 days [Documentary Fact; CP-1]. Rising leverage funded by buybacks: net debt to issuer-adjusted EBITDA of 2.25x against 1.60x, with management comfortable at up to 3x on its covenant definition [Analyst Interpretation; CP-1, CP-1A]. Thin cash: USD 57.0 million of unrestricted cash against USD 96.3 million of restricted cash held for customers [Documentary Fact; CP-1]. Declining revenue: fiscal Q3 revenue down 5.1% and nine-month revenue down 4.4%, with Outside the U.S. guided to break even [Documentary Fact; CP-1, CP-1A]. Lowered outlook and customer modification through December 31, 2026 [Documentary Fact and Management Language; CP-1A]. Floating-rate exposure of USD 978.5 million with a USD 75.0 million swap expiring in September 2026 [Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation; CP-1]. Intangible-heavy balance sheet: goodwill and intangibles USD 2,257.6 million against equity of USD 1,740.6 million [Documentary Fact; CP-1 C14]. Missing creditor protections: Credit Agreement restrictions, amendment terms, guarantors, ratings and ownership detail [Insufficient Information].

runs.text: No acquisition of the issuer, sponsor investment, merger, spin-off, recapitalisation or tender offer is described in the supplied sources, and the context lists no deal terms, quotes or ratings. The transaction row is therefore Insufficient Information, not an adverse conclusion. The financing events in the period under review are ordinary-course bank debt. During fiscal 2025 the company expanded its credit facility by "a $250 million expansion" to support the purchase of 5.8 million shares (10-K page:51); the date and terms of that expansion are not stated in the supplied text. On May 27, 2026 the existing Credit Agreement with J.P. Morgan Chase Bank, N.A. was amended and Term Loan B was increased by 325 million US dollars (Q3 10-Q page:15); the Term Loan B principal moved from 491,250 thousand at March 31, 2026 to 814,173 thousand at June 30, 2026 while the revolver fell from 225,000 to 20,000 thousand (CP-1). Management states that "during fiscal years 2026 and 2025, we expanded our term loans to provide additional capital for our operations, as well as funds to support share repurchases" (Q3 10-Q page:31). The pricing, maturity and covenant terms of the amendment are Not supplied. New interest rate swaps took effect on June 1, 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:16). No bond, note or other debt issue appears in any source, and the Credit Agreement is described as secured by substantially all assets and guaranteed by wholly owned material domestic subsidiaries (10-K page:84). Asset sales are portfolio actions, not financings: the U.S. child support business was sold in December 2025 for approximately 15.0 million US dollars (Q3 10-Q page:15). Subsequent to June 30, 2026, the company declared a quarterly dividend of 0.33 per share on July 6, 2026 (about 17.3 million US dollars, payable August 31, 2026) and collected 245 million US dollars from a delayed federal customer (Q3 10-Q page:22, page:31). No transaction, refinancing or debt issue dated after August 6, 2026 is in the sources.

fields.value: The reported financial base for MAXIMUS, INC. supports a moderately levered, covenant-compliant credit view at June 30, 2026, with the issuer-adjusted measures and the Credit Agreement measures kept apart. Revenue for the nine months ended June 30, 2026 was 3,929,984 thousand against 4,112,861 thousand a year earlier, operating income rose to 456,125 thousand from 405,427 thousand, and issuer-adjusted EBITDA was 550,768 thousand against 541,313 thousand; the operating income gain is largely explained by a 39,343 thousand divestiture charge in the prior-year figure, which the adjusted measure adds back. Net cash used in operating activities was 179,863 thousand against 220,000 thousand, which reflects the seasonal receivables build and, in the current year, delayed payments from a large federal contract, after 1.28 billion US dollars of receivables were sold to a bank. Total debt principal was 1,653,548 thousand against 1,346,875 thousand at September 30, 2025, and unrestricted cash fell to 56,953 thousand from 222,351 thousand, so net debt of 1,596,595 thousand is 2.25 times LTM issuer-adjusted EBITDA of 711,009 thousand (C5), up from 1.60 times. The issuer reports a Credit Agreement ratio of 2.00 against a 4.00 maximum, on its own EBITDA definition that adds 52,278 thousand of pro forma and other adjustments (C9). The stack is a single bank Credit Agreement: Term Loan A, Term Loan B and a 750,000 thousand revolver with 20,000 thousand drawn, secured by substantially all assets (10-K page:84); no bonds or indentures appear in the supplied sources. The nearest large maturity is 690,184 thousand in the year ending September 30, 2029. Open items are the Credit Agreement text and amendment terms, the receivable-sale balance outstanding, letters of credit, and the fiscal fourth quarter, which carries the collections that full-year free cash flow guidance requires (C13).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: MAXIMUS, INC. is a moderately levered, covenant-compliant government services credit whose weak point is seasonal, customer-driven cash flow rather than balance sheet leverage. Its strongest support is a USD 15,327 million backlog at September 30, 2025, a reported covenant leverage ratio of 2.00 against a 4.00 maximum, and bank debt that matures between fiscal 2029 and 2031. The weakest point is that net debt to issuer-adjusted EBITDA rose to 2.25x from 1.60x in nine months, nine-month free cash flow was an outflow of USD 208.6 million, cash is USD 57.0 million, and about 60% of revenue comes from ten contracts. What decides the outcome is whether the fourth-quarter collections that guidance requires arrive, and whether management keeps funding buybacks with debt while a major customer's modification runs to December 31, 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 1. Leverage is moderate but rising. Total debt principal is USD 1,653.5 million and unrestricted cash USD 57.0 million, so net debt is USD 1,596.6 million, or 2.25x LTM issuer-adjusted EBITDA of USD 711.0 million (2.33x gross), against 1.60x at September 30, 2025. Debt principal rose USD 306.7 million and net debt USD 472.1 million in nine months [CP-1 C5, C11].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 2. Covenant headroom is wide on the reported definition. Consolidated net total leverage is 2.00 against a 4.00 maximum, so Credit Agreement EBITDA of USD 798.4 million could fall 50.0% before the test binds, and net interest coverage is 8.72 against a 3.00 minimum, a 65.6% cushion. The Credit Agreement EBITDA exceeds the issuer-adjusted measure by USD 87.4 million of stock compensation and pro forma adjustments, and the agreement and its definitions are not supplied, so the headroom is the issuer's own figure [CP-1 C9; CP-0 gaps].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 3. Cash flow is seasonal and delayed. Operating cash flow was an outflow of USD 179.9 million in nine months and USD 469.5 million for the LTM, 66.0% of issuer-adjusted EBITDA. Days sales outstanding were 98 days against 62 because a large federal contract paid late; USD 245 million was collected after June 30, 2026. Full-year guidance implies fourth-quarter free cash flow of USD 633.6 million to USD 683.6 million, against USD 641.8 million delivered in the prior year's fourth quarter [CP-1 C3, C13; CP-1A].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 4. Shareholder returns are debt-funded. Nine-month buybacks of USD 204.9 million and dividends of USD 51.4 million, USD 256.4 million together, were met from net borrowing of USD 302.7 million and a USD 165.4 million fall in unrestricted cash, with other cash flows not itemised. Fiscal 2025 buybacks of USD 447.5 million were 6.5 times dividends. Management states a target leverage of 2x to 3x on the covenant definition, so the reported 2.00 sits at the bottom of the range [CP-1 C11; CP-1A governance].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 5. Liquidity is adequate but thin in cash. Liquidity is USD 787.0 million: cash USD 57.0 million plus USD 730.0 million of revolver capacity as printed, with letters of credit not stated and the USD 350.0 million receivable-sale facility excluded. Scheduled principal payments are USD 19.0 million for July to September 2026 and USD 75.8 million in fiscal 2027, covered 8.3 times by liquidity; the largest single-year bucket is USD 690.2 million in fiscal 2029 [CP-1 C10, maturities chart].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 6. Interest cost is exposed to floating rates. Swaps cover USD 675.0 million, 40.8% of principal; USD 978.5 million pays SOFR plus margin, so 100 basis points adds about USD 9.8 million a year. A USD 75.0 million Term Loan B swap expires in September 2026. The effective rate is 5.6% [CP-1 C12; C1 below].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 7. Earnings are down and the outlook was lowered. Nine-month revenue was USD 3,930.0 million, 4.4% lower, and fiscal Q3 revenue fell 5.1%, but issuer-adjusted EBITDA margin rose to 14.0% from 13.2%. In August 2026 adjusted EPS guidance fell to USD 7.90 to USD 8.20 from USD 8.25 to USD 8.55 and free cash flow guidance to USD 425 million to USD 475 million from USD 450 million to USD 500 million, after a customer modification effective July 1, 2026 through December 31, 2026 that management expects to reduce diluted EPS by about USD 0.35 per quarter [CP-1 latest quarter; CP-1A timeline].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 8. Revenue is concentrated and terminable. About 55% of fiscal 2025 revenue came from the U.S. federal government, about 60% from the ten largest contracts and about one-fifth from a single federal agency; almost all contracts permit termination for convenience. Backlog of USD 15,327 million is 2.82 times fiscal 2025 revenue but fell 5.2% in the year to September 30, 2025, and no later backlog is supplied [CP-1A operating model, C1, C2].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 9. Claims outside debt are modest but unquantified in places. Operating lease liabilities are USD 94.9 million; receivables of USD 1.28 billion were sold to a bank in nine months with the outstanding balance not printed; performance bonds were USD 33.2 million at September 30, 2025; the MOVEit litigation accrual is not stated; no defined benefit pension is described. Goodwill and intangibles exceed equity by USD 517.0 million [CP-1 claims table, C14].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 10. Governance is open on the facts that matter to creditors. There is no sponsor and no controlling holder disclosed (30 holders of record, about 151,000 beneficial owners), but the proxy statement, Credit Agreement, guarantors and change-of-control terms are not supplied, and three source conflicts are logged: the fiscal 2025 buyback amount, the federal revenue share definition and the Outside the U.S. margin outlook [CP-1A governance and conflicts].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths. Backlog and contract tenure: USD 15,327 million of backlog with about 5.0 years of average remaining life, including options, gives multi-year visibility [Documentary Fact; CP-1A operating model]. Simple, bank-only capital structure: one Credit Agreement with Term Loan A, Term Loan B and a USD 750 million revolver, with no bonds and scheduled principal payments below USD 100 million in each period before fiscal 2029 [Documentary Fact; CP-1 debt register]. Covenant headroom as reported: 2.00 against 4.00 and 8.72 against 3.00 [Documentary Fact, issuer-reported; CP-1]. Cash conversion over a full cycle: fiscal 2025 free cash flow of USD 366.2 million and LTM free cash flow of USD 433.2 million, which includes the prior year's strong fourth quarter [Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation; CP-1 C3]. Margin improvement: issuer-adjusted EBITDA margin of 14.0% in nine months against 13.2%, which management attributes to efficiency initiatives [Management Language; CP-1A operating model]. Light capital intensity: USD 28.8 million of capital expenditure in nine months [Documentary Fact; CP-1]. No sponsor extraction: no related-party leakage or creditor-adverse action is documented, though the legal documents are not supplied [Insufficient Information on legal capacity; CP-1A governance].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weaknesses. Customer and contract concentration: about 60% of revenue from ten contracts, about 55% from the federal government, and termination for convenience in almost all contracts [Documentary Fact; CP-1A]. Seasonal and delayed cash flow: operating cash flow was an outflow of USD 179.9 million in nine months and days sales outstanding were 98 days [Documentary Fact; CP-1]. Rising leverage funded by buybacks: net debt to issuer-adjusted EBITDA of 2.25x against 1.60x, with management comfortable at up to 3x on its covenant definition [Analyst Interpretation; CP-1, CP-1A]. Thin cash: USD 57.0 million of unrestricted cash against USD 96.3 million of restricted cash held for customers [Documentary Fact; CP-1]. Declining revenue: fiscal Q3 revenue down 5.1% and nine-month revenue down 4.4%, with Outside the U.S. guided to break even [Documentary Fact; CP-1, CP-1A]. Lowered outlook and customer modification through December 31, 2026 [Documentary Fact and Management Language; CP-1A]. Floating-rate exposure of USD 978.5 million with a USD 75.0 million swap expiring in September 2026 [Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation; CP-1]. Intangible-heavy balance sheet: goodwill and intangibles USD 2,257.6 million against equity of USD 1,740.6 million [Documentary Fact; CP-1 C14]. Missing creditor protections: Credit Agreement restrictions, amendment terms, guarantors, ratings and ownership detail [Insufficient Information].
